req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET / returns HTTP 200 with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created DESC. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — correct status and presence of known post titles in DESC order; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST /) yields 405; (3) boundary BVA — the topmost post (most recent, id=20 'Heacon signal pulse' 2025-04-01) appears before the second-most-recent (id=19 'Eignal flux ember' 2025-03-16 19:35:10), verifying the ORDER BY created DESC boundary; (4) DT — empty database still returns 200 with no post titles; (5) BVA ordering — the oldest post (id=8 'Sarbor beacon cascade' 2024-11-03) appears last in the rendered HTML relative to a newer post.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_and_post_titles
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with 20 posts and 5 users
actions: Send GET / with Flask test client
expected: Known post titles present in response body
trace: R-FLASKR-001: GET / -> HTTP 200; HTML with post titles
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'text/html' in r.content_type.encode() or b'text/html' in r.headers.get('Content-Type', '').encode()
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data
assert b'Eignal flux ember' in r.data
assert b'Eatrix cascade meridian' in r.data
assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r.data
assert b'Bmber matrix orbit' in r.data
assert b'Sarbor beacon cascade' in r.data

tests.name: test_index_most_recent_post_appears_before_second_most_recent
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with 20 posts ordered by created DESC
Most recent post: id=20 'Heacon signal pulse' 2025-04-01 10:30:37
Second most recent: id=18 'Eatrix cascade meridian' 2025-03-31 18:39:42
actions: Send GET / with Flask test client
Find byte positions of both titles in response body
expected: Byte offset of 'Heacon signal pulse' < byte offset of 'Eatrix cascade meridian'
Byte offset of 'Eatrix cascade meridian' < byte offset of 'Sarbor beacon cascade' (oldest)
trace: R-FLASKR-001: posts ordered by created DESC — boundary between top-1 and top-2
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.data
pos_newest = data.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
pos_second = data.find(b'Eatrix cascade meridian')
pos_oldest = data.find(b'Sarbor beacon cascade')
assert pos_newest != -1, 'Most recent post title not found'
assert pos_second != -1, 'Second most recent post title not found'
assert pos_oldest != -1, 'Oldest post title not found'
assert pos_newest < pos_second, 'Most recent must appear before second most recent'
assert pos_second < pos_oldest, 'Second most recent must appear before oldest'

tests.name: test_index_empty_database_returns_200_no_posts
preconditions: Database initialised with schema but zero post rows
actions: Send GET / with Flask test client against empty post table
expected: Known post titles absent from response body
trace: R-FLASKR-001: boundary — zero posts (lower bound of post count)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert len(r.data) > 0
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' not in r.data
assert b'Pulse ember signal' not in r.data
assert b'Sarbor beacon cascade' not in r.data

tests.name: test_index_ordering_third_and_fourth_most_recent
preconditions: Third most recent: id=19 'Eignal flux ember' 2025-03-16 19:35:10
Fourth most recent: id=1 'Pulse ember signal' 2025-03-16 00:01:36
actions: Send GET / with Flask test client
Compare byte positions of third and fourth most recent titles
expected: Byte offset of 'Eignal flux ember' < byte offset of 'Pulse ember signal'
Confirming DESC ordering at the boundary of same-day posts
trace: R-FLASKR-001: ORDER BY created DESC — same-day boundary between post 19 and post 1
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.data
pos_third = data.find(b'Eignal flux ember')
pos_fourth = data.find(b'Pulse ember signal')
assert pos_third != -1, 'Third most recent post not found'
